subject: Coeus partner: ops playbook request + urgent connector escalation
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@coeus.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Raman <priya@coeus.io>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Coeus connector degraded — logs attached, need runbook + SLA clarity

Hi Jordan,

Quick flag — over the last 24 hours we started seeing a ~30% increase in 502/timeout responses from the Redwood webhook for our batch ingestion. We've collected logs from our side and attached a bundle (coeus-log-bundle-0812.tar.gz). The errors line up with spikes at 02:00 and 07:00 UTC.

This is impacting our nightly import window for three customers; they are querying for RTO/RPO expectations and our success rate dipped below our SLO. We need two things from Redwood today: a concise operational runbook for this integration (who to page, escalation steps, expected time to triage) and confirmation of how your SLA applies when partner-initiated retries are involved (we retry at 3x with exponential backoff).

Can you share a runbook draft and a point person for escalation? I'm looping Priya who owns Coeus integrations.

Thanks,
Liam
Ops Lead — Coeus Integrations

Attachments: coeus-log-bundle-0812.tar.gz (logs, 3.8MB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@coeus.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Raman <priya@coeus.io>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coeus connector degraded — logs attached, need runbook + SLA clarity

Hi Liam — thanks for the quick heads up and for the logs. I pulled the bundle and started an initial triage with infra; preliminary signal points to transient rate-limiting on the edge for requests with long payloads during your bulk imports.

What I can do right away:
- Share a short operational playbook in the next 3 business hours that includes paging steps and the on-call rotation.
- Confirm Redwood's SLA behavior for partner retries — short answer: retries do not extend the SLA window; the original request timestamp is the start of the measurement. I'll get the exact excerpt from the SLA doc.
- Assign an internal owner for the incident: Ben Carter will coordinate with infra and be the primary escalation contact.

Ben: can you take point on tracing the 02:00/07:00 spikes and validate whether autoscaling or external throttles caused queued connections?

Liam/Priya: expect a draft playbook and an excerpted SLA note from me by 13:15 PT. If this is customer-facing high-severity for Coeus customers, say so and we'll elevate to Priority 1.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Partner Success, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam@coeus.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Raman <priya@coeus.io>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 12:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coeus connector degraded — logs attached, need runbook + SLA clarity

Quick update from infra triage:
- I correlated the timestamps Liam provided with edge logs. At 02:03 UTC we observed a short-lived throttle from our API gateway caused by concurrent large POST payloads from Coeus; rate limiter accepted a burst but then started returning 429s which cascaded into timeouts on Coeus side.
- Autoscaling performed but the cold-start delta for the task queue lagged by ~18s during that window.
- No application-level exceptions; this looks capacity/edge-throttle related.

Immediate mitigations I'm recommending:
1) Coeus: stagger bulk imports (simple offset schedule) to avoid synchronized bursts; we can provide a suggested schedule.
2) Redwood: add a partner-specific burst window in the gateway policy for Coeus to raise the temporary throttle ceiling during their nightly windows.
3) Both: short joint runbook that includes who to page (on-call infra), expected triage timeline (15m ack, 90m TTR for escalations to engineering), and contact numbers.

I've prepared a draft playbook and attached a PDF (proposed-coeus-runbook-v1.pdf). Liam — please review and confirm whether the suggested staged import schedule is feasible for you by end of day. If yes, we'll schedule a short ops handshake next week to finalize the gateway burst window.

Attachments: proposed-coeus-runbook-v1.pdf (1.2MB)

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Raman <priya@coeus.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam@coeus.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 16:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coeus connector degraded — logs attached, need runbook + SLA clarity

Thanks, team — the runbook looks good and we validated the staged import schedule with product: we can shift one of the three jobs by 7 minutes to prevent overlap. That's an easy short-term fix.

A few action items from our side:
- Coeus will implement the stagger change tomorrow night (2025-08-15 window).
- Can Redwood implement the partner burst window for Coeus by EOW (2025-08-18)? If not, please state ETA.
- We want a single escalation phone number for after-hours on-call; Jordan/Ben, can you confirm the on-call rotations and provide the number?

If Redwood can commit to the burst window by EOW, we consider this mitigated at customer level and will close the tickets. Otherwise we may need to open a Priority 1 for impacted customers.

Thanks — Priya
Integrations PM, Coeus Integrations
